question: When atomWithStorage receives overlapping promised and direct updates, which authority should govern final atom state and shared storage across one or more Jotai stores?

sources.name: Jotai atomWithStorage implementation
sources.claim: Promised updates call set(baseAtom, resolvedValue) and storage.setItem only after their promise resolves, with no invocation-generation guard.

sources.name: Owned-fork characterization branch
sources.claim: Three target-native controls passed and demonstrate that older promised updates can become final after a newer direct update, reset, or promised update.

review_findings: writeGeneration is a closure variable shared by every store using the same atom definition
store-local atom state and shared storage may require separate authority scopes
generation is assigned after a functional updater executes, permitting reentrant ordering inversion
a newer promised rejection suppressing an older successful promise is untested policy

functional updater that performs a nested write before returning a promise
newer promised update rejects before an older promise resolves

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Maintainers select one global invocation authority across state and storage.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Document cross-store cancellation explicitly and design a global authority mechanism deliberately.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: State authority is per store while storage authority is global.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: One closure counter is insufficient; split the authority model before implementation.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Promised updates intentionally follow resolution order.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Retire the generation candidate and retain the characterization only.

stop_condition: Stop after multi-store, reentrant-updater, and newer-rejection probes yield one explicit authority policy; do not expand into general backend settlement ordering.
